components.note: 口 (mouth) — scaring someone is often done with the voice, a shouted word
下 (xià) gives the sound — it matches this word's reading exactly

example.pinyin: Bié xià wǒ, wǒ dǎnzi hěn xiǎo.
example.english: Don't scare me, I'm very timid.
example.fact: 吓 is the everyday xià; the reading hè survives only in the formal word 恐吓 (to threaten). The pattern 吓一跳 ("get a fright", literally "scared a jump") is the stock way to say something startled you: 我吓了一跳.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — a path runs along the edge or border of something
力 (strength) is just a simplified stand-in for the complicated original right side and carries neither sound nor meaning here

example.pinyin: Yínháng zài xuéxiào de yòubiān.
example.english: The bank is on the right side of the school.
example.fact: 边 is the standard suffix for directions and places: 左边, 右边, 前边, 旁边. It also builds the 边…边… pattern for doing two things at once, as in 边吃边聊 ("chat while eating").

components.note: 又 (hand) appears twice — the simplified form shows two hands, hence a pair

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì shuāng xīn xié.
example.english: I bought a new pair of shoes.
example.fact: 双 is the measure word for things that come as natural pairs: 一双鞋, 一双筷子, 一双手. A single shoe or chopstick is counted with 只 instead. As a prefix it means "double" or "two": 双人床 (double bed), 双语 (bilingual).

components.note: 舌 (tongue) here is a stand-in for the left part of traditional 亂 and does not mean "tongue"
乚 (a bent hook stroke) is the right-hand part kept from the simplification

example.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān tài luàn le.
example.english: My room is too messy.
example.fact: 乱 works as an adjective (房间很乱) and as an adverb before verbs meaning "carelessly, at random": 乱说 (talk nonsense), 乱花钱 (spend money recklessly). 乱七八糟 is the vivid idiom for a total mess.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words are what we speak
司 (sī) gives the sound — a close match for cí

example.pinyin: Zhège cí shì shénme yìsi?
example.english: What does this word mean?
example.fact: 词 is a "word" as a meaningful unit, which may be one or several characters — different from 字, a single written character. That is why dictionaries are 词典 and vocabulary is 词汇. 词 also means song lyrics (歌词).

components.note: ⺈ is the top stroke group of the simplified form, shortened from the original
小 (small) is the lower part kept in the simplified form

example.pinyin: Tā ǒu'ěr huì chídào.
example.english: He is occasionally late.
example.fact: 尔 is the simplified form of 爾 and almost never appears alone in modern Chinese; you meet it in words like 偶尔 (occasionally), 尔后 (afterwards) and in transliterations such as 尔 in foreign place names.

excludeSuggestion: Literary/bound form (simplified 爾) that essentially never stands alone in modern Chinese.

components.note: 走 (walk) — surpassing is a kind of moving past someone
召 (zhào) gives a loose sound hint for chāo

example.pinyin: Tā de chē chāoguò le wǒmen.
example.english: His car overtook us.
example.fact: 超 doubles as a trendy intensifier meaning "super": 超好吃 (super tasty), 超市 (supermarket, "super market"). With a result complement, 超过 means to exceed or overtake.

meanings: measure word for pens and songs

components.note: 十 (ten/cross) is the upper part of the character, a strut-like shape
又 (hand) at the bottom — a hand holding something up, in the traditional reading

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhīchí nǐ de juédìng.
example.english: I support your decision.
example.fact: 支 is a measure word for slender, stick-like things and for songs and teams: 一支笔, 一支歌, 一支队伍. The sense of paying out gives 支付 (to pay) and 支票 (cheque), while 支持 (to support) is a high-frequency verb.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — brush shafts were traditionally made of bamboo
毛 (hair) — a brush tip is made of animal hair

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhī bǐ.
example.english: Please give me a pen.
example.fact: 笔 counts with 支 (一支笔). It also counts strokes of a character, which is why stroke order is 笔顺 and strokes are 笔画. 笔 shows up in 铅笔 (pencil), 钢笔 (fountain pen) and 笔记 (notes).

components.note: 氵 (water) — filling a container with liquid is the classic picture of fullness
The right side now looks like 两 (liǎng) but is a simplified remnant of the old phonetic part that gave the sound mǎn

example.pinyin: Bēizi lǐ zhuāng mǎn le shuǐ.
example.english: The cup is filled with water.
example.fact: 满 is often a result complement showing something is completely full: 装满 (filled up), 坐满 (all seats taken), 写满 (filled with writing). 满意 means "satisfied", and 满 is also the first character of 满族, the Manchu people.

components.note: 亻 (person) — borrowing or pretending is something a person does
叚 (jiǎ) gives the sound, and is also the older form of the "borrow" sense

example.pinyin: Zhè shì jiǎ de, bú shì zhēn de.
example.english: This is fake, not real.
example.fact: The same character has two readings: jiǎ means "fake" (the opposite of 真), while jià means "holiday" (放假, 请假, 暑假). Learners often see 假 in a word and need to check which reading the context calls for.

components.note: 攵 (tap, action) — an action radical: to gather or take something in
丩 (jiū) gives a rough sound hint for shōu

example.pinyin: Wǒ shōudào nǐ de xìn le.
example.english: I received your letter.
example.fact: 收 is a flexible verb of taking in: 收到 (receive), 收钱 (collect money), 收拾 (tidy up), 收藏 (collect as a hobby). The result complement 到 is usually needed for "receive": 收到, not just 收.

components.note: 石 (stone) — smashing is done with a heavy stone or hard object
匝 (zā) gives the sound — nearly identical, differing only in tone

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn zá huài le bēizi.
example.english: He accidentally smashed the cup.
example.fact: 砸 also has a figurative sense of failing: 搞砸了 or 砸了 means "messed up". The idiom 砸锅卖铁 ("smash the pots and sell the iron") means going all-out, giving up everything to achieve something.

components.note: 行 (go, road) — an old picture of a crossroads, which suits a street
圭 (guī) gives only a loose, partial sound hint for jiē

example.hanzi: 周末我们去街上逛逛吧。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jiē shang guàngguang ba.
example.english: Let's go stroll the streets this weekend.
example.fact: 街 is a street with shops and activity, while 路 is a road for getting somewhere, though the two overlap. 逛街 ("wander the streets") is the everyday word for going shopping or hanging out in town. 街 mostly appears in compounds such as 大街, 街上, 街道.

components.note: 匸 (a box-like enclosure) marks off a bounded space
乂 (crossed strokes) is what remains inside the box after simplification

example.pinyin: Zhège qū de jiāotōng hěn fāngbiàn.
example.english: Transport in this district is very convenient.
example.fact: 区 is a district or zone, as in 朝阳区 (a Beijing district), 郊区 (suburb), 地区 (region) and 小区 (residential compound). Careful: 区别 is read qūbié, and the surname Ōu uses the same character with a different reading.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the radical for hand actions such as hitting and pushing
童 (tóng) gives a loose sound hint for zhuàng

example.pinyin: Wǒ de chē bèi zhuàng le.
example.english: My car got hit.
example.fact: 撞 is a more forceful hit than 碰 (to touch or bump lightly). 撞见 means to run into someone unexpectedly, often catching them doing something, and 撞车 covers both a car crash and a clash of schedules or ideas.

components.note: 亻 (person) — lending and borrowing happen between people
昔 (xī) gives a loose sound hint for jiè

example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ jiè nǐ de bǐ ma?
example.english: May I borrow your pen?
example.fact: 借 means both "borrow" and "lend", a classic source of confusion. Direction is shown by context: 借我 / 向你借 means borrow, while 借给我 means lend to me. Many people add 给 or 出 to make the lending meaning clear.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the original sense was the fine awn of a grain plant
少 (shǎo) gives the sound — it rhymes with miǎo

example.pinyin: Zhège hóngdēng hái yǒu shí miǎo.
example.english: This red light has ten seconds left.
example.fact: 秒 started as a tiny grain tip, an image of something very small, which became the unit "second". In internet slang it is a prefix for instant: 秒懂 (get it instantly), 秒回 (reply right away), 秒杀 (flash sale).

components.note: 车 (cart) — the older sense is transporting goods by vehicle
俞 (yú) gives the sound — a close match for shū

example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì shū le bǐsài.
example.english: Our team lost the match.
example.fact: 输 means "to lose" a contest or bet, the opposite of 赢. Its original meaning of carrying goods lives on in 运输 (transport) and 输入 / 输出 (input / output), and 输液 means to get an IV drip.

meanings: measure word for mountains and buildings

components.note: 广 (a building with a roof) — a covered place
坐 (to sit) — together they suggest a place to sit

example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zhège zuòwèi yǒu rén ma?
example.english: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
example.fact: 座 is a seat, but it is also the measure word for large, fixed things: 一座山, 一座桥, 一座城市. It appears in 座位 (seat), 讲座 (lecture) and in star-sign names like 天蝎座.

components.note: 咸 (xián) is the upper part, stacked above the heart
心 (heart) — the heart radical shows this is about feelings

example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎndào hěn gāoxìng.
example.english: I feel very happy.
example.fact: 感 attaches to many nouns as a suffix meaning "sense of": 安全感 (sense of security), 幸福感 (happiness), 责任感 (responsibility). It also builds 感觉 (to feel), 感谢 (thank) and 感冒 (to catch a cold).

components.note: Originally a picture of a winnowing basket (later written 箕); the pronoun sense is a borrowed use of the same character

example.hanzi: 其中有一个是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: Qízhōng yǒu yí gè shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: One of them is my friend.
example.fact: 其 is a classical pronoun meaning "his / her / its / their" that survives mostly in fixed words: 其中 (among them), 其他 (other), 其实 (actually), 尤其 (especially), 其次 (secondly). It is rarely used as a free word in speech.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — hatred is an emotion of the heart
艮 (gèn) gives the sound — it only differs in initial

example.hanzi: 我恨自己没有早点告诉你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hèn zìjǐ méiyǒu zǎodiǎn gàosu nǐ.
example.english: I hate myself for not telling you sooner.
example.fact: 恨 is stronger than 讨厌 (to dislike) and carries real resentment or regret. The pattern 恨不得 ("hate that one cannot") expresses an intense wish: 我恨不得马上回家, "I can't wait to go home right now".

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — shedding skin or removing something from the body
兑 (duì) gives only a loose sound hint for tuō

example.pinyin: Jìn mén qǐng tuō xié.
example.english: Please take off your shoes when you come in.
example.fact: 脱 is the verb for removing clothes, shoes and hats (opposite of 穿 or 戴). Figuratively it means getting free of something: 脱离 (break away from), 脱口而出 (blurt out), and the slang 脱单 ("leave singlehood").

components.note: 阝 (a mound radical, written on the left) is the traditional radical here; its link to "accompany" is faint
咅 gives a loose sound hint for péi

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ péi māma qù kànbìng.
example.english: On the weekend I go with my mother to see the doctor.
example.fact: 陪 always needs a person to accompany: 陪我, 陪孩子玩, 陪客人. It implies keeping someone company for their sake, unlike 跟, which just means "with". 陪伴 is a warmer, more literary "companionship".

components.note: A picture of grains of rice or millet scattered around a central line

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu chī mǐfàn.
example.english: I eat rice every day.
example.fact: 米 is uncooked rice or grain, while cooked rice is 饭 (米饭). It is also the everyday word for the metre: 一米八 (1.8 metres) is how people give their height, and 百米 is the 100-metre race.

meanings: prefix before names and kin terms

components.note: 阝 (a mound radical) — the original sense of 阿 was a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a loose sound hint for the old reading of 阿

example.pinyin: Āyí, nǐ hǎo!
example.english: Hello, auntie!
example.fact: 阿 is a friendly prefix before names and family words: 阿姨 (auntie), 阿姐, 阿明. It is also used to transcribe foreign sounds, as in 阿根廷 (Argentina) and 阿富汗 (Afghanistan).

excludeSuggestion: Functions almost only as a prefix or transliteration syllable, rarely as a standalone word.

components.note: Thought to show a flame sitting on a lamp stand; the sense of "master" or "main" is an extension of the standing flame

example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè jiā diàn de zhǔrén.
example.english: He is the owner of this shop.
example.fact: 主 means the one in charge or the main thing: 主人 (host, owner), 主要 (main), 主意 (idea, decision), 主任 (director). 主意 is a good one to know: 拿主意 means "make up one's mind".

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat comes from fire
执 (zhí) gives only a loose sound hint for rè

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn rè.
example.english: The weather is very hot today.
example.fact: 热 describes heat of weather, food and drinks, whereas very hot to the touch is 烫. It also means "popular": 热门 (hot topic), 热销 (selling well), and 热闹 means lively and bustling. Drinking 热水 (hot water) is a daily habit in China.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) at the top — the pieces do not clearly show the meaning
工 (work) at the bottom — the character's original form is hard to read directly

example.pinyin: Xiànzài chà wǔ fēn bā diǎn.
example.english: It's five to eight now.
example.fact: 差 has three readings: chà (poor, lacking), chā (difference, as in 差别) and chāi (errand, as in 出差). Chà is how you tell time: 差五分八点 means "five minutes short of eight". 差不多 (almost the same) is read chà too.

components.note: Simplified form of 盡; the parts 尺 and ⺀ are shorthand that do not carry a clear meaning of their own

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng jìnlì le.
example.english: I have already done my best.
example.fact: 尽 has two readings: jìn means to exhaust or do to the fullest (尽力, 用尽), while jǐn means "as much as possible" (尽快, 尽量). Learners often read 尽快 with jìn by mistake; it is jǐnkuài, "as soon as possible".

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — an island is a place in the sea where birds land
山 (mountain) — an island rises like a mountain out of the water

example.hanzi: 我们坐船去了一个小岛。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán qù le yí gè xiǎo dǎo.
example.english: We took a boat to a small island.
example.fact: 岛 counts with 座 (一座岛) as well as 个. It builds 半岛 (peninsula, "half island"), 群岛 (archipelago) and 岛国 (island nation), and 台湾岛 is the main island of Taiwan.

components.note: 饣 (food) — being hungry is lacking food
我 (wǒ) gives the sound — a near match for è

example.pinyin: Wǒ è le, wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: I'm hungry, let's go eat.
example.fact: 饿 is hungry and is usually followed by 了 to show a change of state: 我饿了 means "I've become hungry". Intensify it with 饿死了 ("starving to death"), and note 饿 can also be a verb: 别饿着孩子, "don't let the child go hungry".

components.note: 纟 (silk) — red was a prized silk dye colour
工 (gōng) gives the sound — a close match for hóng

example.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn hóng yīfu.
example.english: She is wearing a red top.
example.fact: 红 is a lucky colour in China, used for weddings, New Year and 红包 (red envelopes of money). It also means popular: 走红 (to become popular), 网红 (internet celebrity). On Chinese stock charts red means prices going up, the opposite of Western convention.

components.note: 又 (hand) replaced the complicated original right side in the simplified form
鸟 (bird) — a chicken is a kind of bird

example.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnfàn xiǎng chī jīròu.
example.english: I want chicken for dinner.
example.fact: 鸡 counts with 只 (一只鸡). It is the tenth sign of the Chinese zodiac, rendered in English as Rooster. 鸡蛋 is egg, and 鸡 shows up in food words like 炸鸡 (fried chicken) and 宫保鸡丁 (kung pao chicken).

components.note: 羊 (yáng) gives the sound — a near match for yǎng
儿 (person) stands in for the "food" part of the traditional form: feeding someone to raise them

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǎng le yì zhī māo.
example.english: I keep a cat.
example.fact: 养 is used for raising pets (养猫), plants (养花), children (养孩子) and even recovering (养病). 养成习惯 means to form a habit, and 养 is the verb to feed or support a family: 养家.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — chasing is moving after someone
The right part, a form of 𠂤 (duī), gives a rough sound hint for zhuī

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài zhuī xiǎotōu.
example.english: The police are chasing the thief.
example.fact: 追 goes well beyond literal chasing: 追求 means to pursue (a goal, or romantically), 追剧 means to binge a TV series, and 追星 means to follow a celebrity. 追上 is to catch up with.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — thanks are spoken
射 (shè) gives the sound — they share the same vowel

example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de bāngzhù.
example.english: Thank you for your help.
example.fact: 谢 is thanks, usually doubled as 谢谢; the reply is 不谢 ("no thanks needed"). It is also a surname, the verb for withering flowers (花谢了), and 谢绝 means to politely refuse.

meanings: measure word for flocks and groups

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — sheep live in flocks, so a flock is the original picture
君 (jūn) gives the sound — they share the same vowel

example.pinyin: Yì qún háizi zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
example.english: A group of kids is playing in the park.
example.fact: 群 is a measure word for flocks and crowds of people, animals or things: 一群鸟, 一群人. 人群 means crowd, and in modern life 群 is a chat group: 微信群 (WeChat group).

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) surrounds the character
大 (big, or a person with arms spread) sits inside — a common reading is a person resting on a mat

example.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒmen méi qù.
example.english: Because it rained, we didn't go.
example.fact: 因 rarely stands alone; it pairs with 为 in 因为…所以… (because…so…). It also forms 因此 (therefore), 原因 (reason) and 因素 (factor).

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — binding together, as an agreement binds people
勺 (sháo) gives only a loose sound hint for yuē

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yuēhǎo míngtiān jiànmiàn.
example.english: We have arranged to meet tomorrow.
example.fact: 约 means to arrange to meet (约朋友, 约好) and also the resulting appointment, as in 有约. It additionally means "approximately" (大约) and "agreement" (合约, 条约). 约会 is a date.

components.note: 走 (walk) — moving quickly to catch up
干 (gān) gives the sound — it only differs in tone

example.pinyin: Wǒ děi gǎn huǒchē, kuài zǒu ba.
example.english: I have to catch the train, let's go.
example.fact: 赶 means to hurry to catch something: 赶火车, 赶时间 (be in a hurry). 赶上 means to make it in time, 赶不上 means to miss it. As a different sense it can mean to drive away, as in 赶走.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — slowness can be a matter of attitude or patience
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Qǐng shuō màn yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please speak a bit slower.
example.fact: 慢 is the opposite of 快. 慢走 ("walk slowly") is what a host says as you leave, meaning "take care", and 慢慢来 means "take your time". Put 慢 after the verb to ask someone to slow down: 说慢一点.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — thunder comes with storms
田 (field) is a remnant of the older rumbling-wheels shape, not a literal field

example.pinyin: Zuówǎn dǎléi le, wǒ shuì bù zháo.
example.english: There was thunder last night, so I couldn't sleep.
example.fact: 雷 is thunder (打雷), and also underlies 地雷 (landmine) and 雷达 (radar, a sound-meaning transliteration). In slang 雷人 means shocking or cringe-worthy, and 雷 is a surname.

components.note: 火 (fire) — burning is done with fire
尧 (yáo) gives a loose sound hint for shāo

example.pinyin: Tā fāshāo le, yào chī yào.
example.english: He has a fever and needs to take medicine.
example.fact: 烧 is used for burning (烧纸), heating (烧水 to boil water) and certain ways of cooking (红烧 braising in soy sauce). 发烧 is "to run a fever", literally "to emit burning".

components.note: 石 (stone) — smashing something with a stone
皮 (pí) gives a loose sound hint for pò

example.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī píngmù pò le.
example.english: My phone screen is broken.
example.fact: 破 is broken or torn (破了) and a verb for breaking through: 打破纪录 (break a record). Before nouns it can be dismissive, as in 破车 (a lousy old car). 破费 is a polite phrase meaning "spend money", as in 让您破费了.

components.note: 氵 (water) — clean, clear water
青 (qīng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de shuǐ hěn qīng.
example.english: The water in this river is very clear.
example.fact: 清 means clear in the sense of clean water, but also clear in understanding: 清楚 (clear), 看清楚 (see clearly). It is also the name of the Qing dynasty (1644–1912), written with the same character.

components.note: 夕 (evening) is the core part — night follows the evening

example.pinyin: Yè lǐ hěn ānjìng.
example.english: It's very quiet at night.
example.fact: 夜 is night as a span of time; in everyday speech people more often say 晚上 (evening/night). 夜 appears in 夜里 (at night), 夜市 (night market, a beloved institution), 夜宵 (late-night snack) and 熬夜 (to stay up late).

components.note: 氵 (water) — the original sense was flowing water spreading out, a meaning that extended to "develop"
寅 (yín) gives the sound — a close match for yǎn

example.hanzi: 他在这部电影里演医生。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǎn yīshēng.
example.english: He plays a doctor in this film.
example.fact: 演 takes the role directly as its object: 演医生 means "play a doctor". It is the root of 表演 (perform), 演员 (actor), 演出 (a show), 演讲 (speech) and 演唱会 (concert).

components.note: Two stacked parts, 尸 and 匕; the meaning "nun" comes from transliterating Sanskrit bhikṣuṇī as 比丘尼

example.hanzi: 那位尼姑住在山上的寺里。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi nígū zhù zài shān shàng de sì lǐ.
example.english: That nun lives in a temple on the mountain.
example.fact: 尼 alone means a Buddhist nun, but you will mostly meet it as a sound syllable in transliterations: 尼泊尔 (Nepal), 尼日利亚 (Nigeria), 尼龙 (nylon). 尼姑 is the standard word for a nun.

excludeSuggestion: Mostly a transliteration syllable (Nepal, nylon, etc.), rarely a standalone word.
